$comment: ProtoFlow component catalog: what each built-in Grove component registers, and the exact values a web app receives from it or sends to it. Single source for components.md, the virtual kit and the demo page. Edit this file, then run `node dev/scripts/build-components-doc.js`, which checks it against the firmware and regenerates components.md.
rules: Names are chosen in the sketch. The names below are the ones the example sketches use. Components that register several sensors build the names from the instance name: `climate` gives `climate_temp` and `climate_humidity`.

Receive sensor data: subscribe to the device, then `ProtoFlow.on('sensor', ({ device, sensor, value, timestamp }) => ...)`. `sensor` is the registered name, and `value` has the form listed for that sensor.

Numbers sent in compact form arrive rounded to two decimals. Numbers sent as JSON (for example the joystick axes, which share a type) can have more, so round them before display. On/off sensors arrive as `true` or `false`.
The example sketches send each sensor's current value once the device has registered, then again whenever it changes. The change threshold and the rate are set in the sketch.

The device list (`ProtoFlow.on('devices', ...)`) carries each sensor and actuator as the device registered it: `name`, `type`, `data_type`, `unit` and `description` when set, and `min_value` / `max_value` for `float` and `int` only. A UI can set itself up from it. (The `min` and `max` below are what the sketch passes, including for other types.)
Send a command: `ProtoFlow.sendCommand(deviceUuid, actuatorName, value)`, with a `value` from that actuator's command list. Send each command as its own message, exactly as listed.

On/off actuators (types `led` and `buzzer`) take `true` / `false`, `1` / `0` or `"on"` / `"off"`. Node-RED reads the strings `"on"`, `"1"` and `"true"` (any case) as on and every other string as off. Any other value is on when it is truthy, so every number except 0 means on.
`rgb_led` and `tone_buzzer` commands are packed into a short code on the way to the device. Only `{r, g, b}` and `{frequency, duration}` get through, so always send exactly those fields, as numbers.
Don't put two actuators of the same type on one device: a command always reaches the first one. `GroveVibrator` and `GroveBuzzer` are both `buzzer`; `GroveLED` and `GroveLEDButton` are both `led`.
Components marked untested have not been verified on hardware yet.

components.summary: Slider position as a percentage.

components.module: Grove - Rotary Angle Sensor v1.2 / (P) v1.2
components.summary: Knob position as a percentage of its 300-degree turn.

sensors.name: knob
sensors.value: Number 0-100: the knob's position across its 300-degree turn.

components.summary: Push button, debounced.
notes: The GroveDualButton example shows two buttons on one device (`button_a`, `button_b`).

components.summary: Two-axis stick with a push button.

sensors.name: joystick_button
sensors.value: `true` while the stick is pressed down.

notes: `joystick_button` is registered only when the sketch enables the button (the example does).
Calibrate the centre and the ends with the GroveThumbJoystickCalibration example.

components.module: Grove - PIR Motion Sensor / Mini PIR Motion Sensor v1.8
components.summary: Detects movement of people and animals.
notes: Needs a warm-up after power-on (30 s in the example) and reports `false` until then.

components.module: Grove - Sound Sensor v1.6 / Loudness Sensor
components.summary: Loudness of the surroundings.
Distance to the nearest object in front of the sensor.

components.module: Grove - Temperature & Humidity Sensor (DHT11, blue) / Pro (DHT22, white)
components.summary: Air temperature and relative humidity from one module.
notes: The sensor can be read at most every 2 s. Both values are re-sent every 10 s even when they don't change.
For the white Pro module, set `dhtType = DHT22` in the sketch.

components.summary: Acceleration along three axes; at rest it shows gravity, so it also tells tilt.

sensors.name: accelerometer
sensors.value: Object `{accel: {x, y, z}}`, each in g. Lying flat and still: about `z = 1`.

notes: Only one IMU-type sensor per device is supported.

components.summary: Recognises hand gestures in front of the sensor.

sensors.name: gesture
sensors.value: One of `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `forward`, `backward`, `clockwise`, `counterclockwise`, `wave`. Sent once per detected gesture; there is no initial value.

components.summary: A single LED, on or off.
notes: On/off only, no brightness. Also accepts `1` / `0` and `"on"` / `"off"`.

components.summary: Ten LEDs in a row, for levels and bar graphs.

commands.effect: Level 0-10, lit from one end like a bar graph
Each of the 10 LEDs on (1) or off (0)

components.summary: Full-colour LED; several can be chained, and all show the same colour.
notes: Only `r`, `g` and `b` reach the device (see the `rgb_led` rule above).

components.module: Grove - RGB LED Stick (10 WS2813 Mini LEDs)
components.summary: Ten full-colour LEDs, each settable on its own.
notes: The device acts on the first key it recognises, so put one command in each message.

components.summary: Small vibration motor, on or off.
notes: Registers as type `buzzer`, so don't combine it with `GroveBuzzer` on one device.

components.summary: Loud beeper at a fixed pitch (about 2.3 kHz).
notes: Switches itself off after 5 s (`maxOnMs` in the sketch).
Registers as type `buzzer`, so don't combine it with `GroveVibrator` on one device.

components.summary: Plays notes at a chosen pitch; louder and lower than the buzzer.

commands.effect: Play a note: frequency in Hz, duration in ms (at most 5 s)

notes: Send both fields (see the `tone_buzzer` rule above).
Needs 5 V. Low notes sound best; the volume knob is on the board.

components.summary: Four 7-segment digits with a colon.

commands.effect: Text; only characters a 7-segment display can show

components.module: Grove - LCD RGB Backlight v4.0 (16 x 2 characters)
components.summary: Two lines of text with a colour backlight.
Small monochrome screen for text and a progress bar.
Push button with a built-in LED that the web app can switch.
notes: Its LED is type `led`, so don't combine it with `GroveLED` on one device.

components.summary: Plays MP3 files from an SD card and reports what it is doing.

sensors.name: mp3_status
sensors.value: Object `{playing, volume, mode}`, every 2 s while status reporting is on.

commands.effect: Track number 3 from the SD card's root
song.mp3 from the SD card's root

notes: Needs an SD card (FAT32) with MP3 files.
The header comment also lists `currentTime` and `totalTime` in the status, but the code doesn't send them.
